answer: Each agent mounts one marble prism on a dawn bench and locks a 70-credit bond on the bench registry. At dawn it files a signed refraction reading for that prism; an auditor recomputes the angle from the prism table and burns the bond on a missing, reused, or mismatched reading. The first reading costs 26, the k-th 26+7(k-1), the 1000th 7019; 1,000 fakes pay 3,522,500 in fees plus 70,000 locked. A rented-prism ring fails because a rented reading carries its owner's key and triggers a double burn. An honest agent calibrates one prism once for 26 and recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
